Hi Sean / Marissa,

Quick ask from our side — we are hoping to onboard a telemetry subvendor, ByteLens (contact: Elena Park, legal@bytelens.io), to handle log aggregation and short-term storage for Terradrift traces ingested by Redwood for the Terradrift integration. ByteLens will only process non-personally-identifiable telemetry and operational logs; they will not receive model inputs or customer PII.

Terradrift is requesting:
- a flow-down notice or Order Form amendment that authorizes ByteLens as a subvendor,
- confirmation that the ByteLens DPA/SSA is acceptable to Redwood, and
- a short list of evidentiary items (SOC2 or equivalent, encryption-in-transit confirmation).

Attached: bytelens-ssa.pdf (vendor security summary). Can you advise the path forward and expected timeline? We need to close procurement by 11/13 to keep the integration window.

Thanks,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: add ByteLens as subvendor for telemetry pipeline

Sean / Marissa / Elena — I reviewed the ByteLens SSA and have the following notes. High-level: the vendor appears low-to-medium risk for the intended telemetry scope, but we need to capture flow-down and minimal contractual protections. Proposed approach below to keep the procurement window.

1) Prefer Order Form amendment over MSA-level wholesale edits. Add a short clause to the Order Form that: (i) names ByteLens as an authorized subprocessor for the Terradrift integration; (ii) requires ByteLens to comply with the data processing restrictions in Redwood's DPA; and (iii) gives Redwood the right to require remedial measures "as reasonably necessary" if ByteLens materially fails to comply. Suggested language: "ByteLens, Inc. (\"Subprocessor\") is authorized to process telemetry on behalf of Customer under the terms of the Agreement provided that Subprocessor executes an SSA consistent with the DPA and maintains security controls appropriate to the processing activities."

2) DPA/SSA: the attached SSA is largely acceptable but lacks explicit encryption-in-transit wording for aggregated logs and a minimum retention cap. Ask ByteLens to insert: "\"Subprocessor shall encrypt Customer data in transit using TLS 1.2+ and shall not retain telemetry beyond 90 days unless explicitly authorized by Customer.\""

3) Evidence: we can provide a short evidentiary bundle to Terradrift procurement: (a) current SOC 2 Type II report OR equivalent attestation; (b) encryption-in-transit confirmation (one-pager); (c) contact for breach/incident notification. If ByteLens cannot provide SOC 2, accept a recent security questionnaire + live security call.

4) Liability / indemnity: do not accept broad subcontractor indemnities. Keep the Order Form amendment limited to scope and remedial rights; do not carve Redwood out of any limitation-of-liability protections in the MSA.

5) DocuSign/route: I will prepare a short redline for the Order Form amendment (PDF) and a DPA addendum suggestion. Marissa — please confirm procurement routing (DocuSign envelope or internal routing) and I will attach the redline. Target for internal signoff: EOD Monday 2026-11-09 so Terradrift can sign by 11/13.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Legal — Contracts & Privacy
